subject: Request: Full removal of prompts & outputs (Medisys Prod)
messages:
From: Oliver Chen <oliver.chen@medisys.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
Cc: compliance@medisys.com
Date: 2026-06-14T08:12:00Z
Subject: Request: Full removal of prompts & outputs (Medisys Prod)

Hi Priya,

Per Section 4.2 of our Data Processing Addendum and our internal retention obligations, Medisys is requesting a full removal of all prompt inputs, generated outputs, and associated inference logs produced by our production tenant (tenant id: medisys-prod-01) between 2025-01-01 and 2026-06-13.

Goals:
- Complete purge of prompt/store artifacts and any cached KV artifacts tied to Medisys identifiers.
- Remove any derived embeddings or indexes generated from customer data.
- Provide verifiable proof artifacts we can retain for our audit.

Can you confirm:
1) The steps Redwood will take and which storage layers will be touched (KV cache, object store, index service, audit logs).
2) Expected ETA for completion and when we can expect a signed proof package.
3) Any limitations (e.g., immutable audit trails required by law) or items that cannot be expunged.

We need the deletion to be complete and evidence delivered by EOD 2026-06-16 to meet our compliance window. Please advise next steps.

Thanks,
Oliver Chen
Head of Security Operations
Medisys Health
From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: Oliver Chen <oliver.chen@medisys.com>
Cc: compliance@medisys.com, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-14T09:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: Full removal of prompts & outputs (Medisys Prod)

Hi Oliver — thanks for the clear request and the target date. I’ve looped in Marcus (Ops) and Naomi (Security) to coordinate execution and evidence.

High-level plan we propose (I want to confirm with you before starting):
1) Ticketize all affected systems and create a single-run sweep job: KV cache (ephemeral memory + checkpoint blobs), prompt-output store (S3: redwood-med-prod/medisys/), embeddings index (vector-service indices tagged medisys_prod_01), and inference logs (log-shipper -> cold storage).
2) Quarantine affected artifacts, perform deletion, and then run a verification sweep that produces a manifest of removed object keys and cryptographic hashes of evidence files.
3) Produce a signed proof package (proof_of_deletion_manifest.zip) and an internal ops report (sweep_report_20260615.csv). We'll also include a short runbook of the commands executed for your auditors.

Questions for Medisys:
- Are there any specific object prefixes or customer IDs beyond the tenant id above we should include? (helps avoid under/over deleting)
- Do you require any notarization or a third-party witness for the proof package?

If you confirm, Marcus will start the sweep prep today. ETA: preliminary manifest by 2026-06-15 morning, final signed delivery by EOD 2026-06-15 if no blockers.

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-06-14T11:40:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: Full removal of prompts & outputs (Medisys Prod)

Priya / team — initiating ops detail.

Summary of execution steps (for internal and customer transparency):
- Systems in scope:
  * KV cache service (in-memory + periodic snapshots) — keys tagged with tenant=medisys-prod-01
  * Prompt-output object store — S3 bucket redwood-med-prod (prefix: medisys/2025-01-01_to_2026-06-13/)
  * Embeddings service — indices with tag medisys_prod_01; we will delete index shards and rewrite any composite catalogs referencing those vectors.
  * Inference logging pipeline — remove messages from hot store and mark records for purge from cold storage; immutable audit logs will be marked but not removed if retention is contractually required.

Planned timeline (subject to resource lock):
- 2026-06-14 12:00 UTC: Acquire deletion token and snapshot current state.
- 2026-06-14 13:00–18:00 UTC: Execute deletion across systems (batched to avoid service impact).
- 2026-06-15 02:00 UTC: Run verification sweep to collect removed keys and hashes.
- 2026-06-15 08:00 UTC: Produce sweep_manifest_20260614.txt and sweep_report_20260615.csv; sign proof_of_deletion_manifest.zip with our HSM key.

Notes / caveats:
- Immutable audit trails required by some regulators are stored separately; we will provide access logs and redaction notes but cannot remove the root audit record without explicit legal exception.
- Derived telemetry (aggregates that cannot be traced to individual records) will remain.

I’ll attach the initial manifest when the first sweep completes.

Subject: Re: Request: Full removal of prompts & outputs (Medisys Prod) — sweep evidence attached

Hi Oliver — attaching the artifact package from the sweep. Files included:
- sweep_manifest_20260614.txt (list of object keys removed)
- sweep_report_20260615.csv (per-system result rows: object_key, system, operation, timestamp, operator)
- proof_of_deletion_manifest.zip (signed with Redwood HSM key; contains lightweight proof files and hashes)

Attachments: [sweep_manifest_20260614.txt (TXT)], [sweep_report_20260615.csv (CSV)], [proof_of_deletion_manifest.zip (ZIP)]

Summary: deletion run completed and verification sweep succeeded. A few items to note:
- We could not remove immutable audit ledger entries; these are documented in the manifest under column "audit_exemption_reason".
- Vector index shards referencing Medisys vectors were deleted and composite catalogs rewritten; the CSV shows shard ids removed.
- We recorded cryptographic hashes for the deleted objects; hashes are inside the zip.

Next steps for closure: please reply to this thread confirming receipt and acceptance of the proof package. If you require notarization we can coordinate a third-party witness (extra lead time).

Thanks — Priya

--
Priya Natarajan

Priya / Marcus — thank you. We confirm receipt of the proof package and manifest. Our compliance team will ingest the ZIP and hashes for the audit.

1) The "audit_exemption_reason" lines look reasonable. Please include a short blurb in the final runbook explaining why those records are preserved.
